name: OPNsense - SSH Brute Force Detection
description: More than 10 SSH connections blocked from the same source IP within 5 minutes. Indicator of brute force attack.
author: OPNsense SOC Team
note:
## SSH Brute Force Detection

### Immediate Steps
1. Block source IP: {{context.source.ip}} manually on OPNsense
2. Check SSH logs on target system: /var/log/auth.log
3. Verify if any successful login exists (Event: Accepted password/publickey)
4. Add fail2ban or OPNsense IDS rule

name: OPNsense - RDP Brute Force Detection
description: More than 10 RDP connections blocked from the same source IP within 5 minutes. Indicator of brute force attack.
author: OPNsense SOC Team
note:
## RDP Brute Force Detection

### Immediate Steps
1. Block source IP: {{context.source.ip}}
2. Check Windows Event Log on target system (Event ID 4625 - Failed Logon)
3. Do not expose RDP directly to the internet — place it behind a VPN
4. Enforce NLA (Network Level Authentication)

name: OPNsense - Port Scan Detection
description: Same source IP attempted more than 15 different ports within 5 minutes. Indicator of network reconnaissance / port scanning.
author: OPNsense SOC Team
note:
## Port Scan Detection

### Analysis
- Review scanned ports in Kibana
- Single target IP indicates service discovery; multiple targets indicate network mapping

### Steps
1. Check source IP geolocation
2. Trigger IDS/IPS rule
3. Temporarily block source IP on OPNsense

name: OPNsense - DDoS / Traffic Flood (Inbound)
description: Triggered when more than 500 packets reach a single destination within 1 minute. Detects flood attacks from both internal and external sources.
query: destination.ip: * AND network.direction: "out" OR destination.ip: * AND network.direction: "in"
author: OPNsense SOC Team
note:
## URGENT Response — DDoS

### Detection
- Target IP: {{context.destination.ip}}
- Packet count: {{context.hits.total}}

### Steps
1. Rate-limit incoming traffic to target IP on OPNsense
2. Identify source IPs: Kibana → opnsense-syslog-*
3. Request blackhole routing from upstream ISP
4. Redirect to CDN/scrubbing center

name: OPNsense - SMB Lateral Movement / Ransomware Indicator
description: Same internal source IP established SMB (port 445) connections to more than 3 different targets within 10 minutes. Indicator of ransomware propagation or lateral movement.
author: OPNsense SOC Team
note:
## SMB Lateral Movement / Ransomware URGENT

### Steps
1. IMMEDIATELY isolate the source system from the network
2. Check EDR/AV logs
3. Inspect affected SMB target systems
4. Verify if shadow copies have been deleted
5. Activate Incident Response plan

name: OPNsense - Abnormal TCP Flag Combination Detection
description: Suspicious TCP flag combinations detected (NULL scan, FIN scan, XMAS scan). Possible firewall bypass or covert port scanning attempt.
author: OPNsense SOC Team
note:
## Abnormal TCP Flag Detection

### Flag Types
- NULL scan (0x000): All flags off — RFC violation
- FIN scan: FIN only — RST returned on closed ports
- XMAS scan (SF): SYN+FIN together — invalid combination

### Steps
1. Monitor source IP
2. Analyze target ports
3. Create IDS signature

name: OPNsense - High Risk Country Connection Detection
description: Blocked connections from high-risk countries (RU, CN, KP, IR, SY, BY, CU) exceeded 3 within 15 minutes.
query: source.geo.country_iso_code: (RU OR CN OR KP OR IR OR SY OR BY OR CU) AND event.action: "block"
author: OPNsense SOC Team
note:
## High Risk Country Detection

### Monitored Countries: RU CN KP IR SY BY CU

### Steps
1. Inspect target port — is it a critical service?
2. Configure country-based geo-blocking on OPNsense: Firewall → Aliases → GeoIP
3. Request upstream BGP null-route if necessary

name: OPNsense - Database Port Scan Detection
description: Same source IP scanned more than 3 different database ports within 5 minutes. Indicator of data exfiltration preparation or CVE exploit search.
query: destination.port: (1433 OR 3306 OR 5432 OR 6379 OR 27017 OR 9200 OR 5984 OR 9042)
author: OPNsense SOC Team
note:
## Database Port Scan Detection

### Scanned Ports
1433:MSSQL | 3306:MySQL | 5432:PostgreSQL | 6379:Redis | 27017:MongoDB | 9200:Elasticsearch | 5984:CouchDB | 9042:Cassandra

### Steps
1. Restrict DB server access to internal network only
2. Block source IP
3. Check DB server authentication logs
